newsitem.title: USA: U.S. productivity up 0.6 percent in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. productivity up 0.6 percent in second quarter.

text.p: Productivity gains at American businesses slowed in the second quarter and were slower in the first quarter than previously estimated, the Labour Department said on Tuesday.

Productivity outside the farm sector rose at a 0.6 percent annual rate in the second quarter, down from a 1.4 percent rate in the first quarter, the department said. It had previously estimated productivity rose at a 2.6 percent rate in the first quarter.
Wall Street economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 0.7 percent gain in second-quarter productivity and a 2.7 percent jump in unit labour costs.
Unit labour costs, which figure heavily in the prices of goods and services, rose at a 2.4 percent rate in the second quarter after a 3.1 percent first-quarter gain, the report said.

Federal Reserve policy-makers, set to meet next week to decide their next move on interest rates, watch data on labour costs and productivity closely. Higher productivity allows companies to boost worker pay and benefits without forcing price hikes or eating into profits.

Productivity, a measure of business efficiency based on output of goods and services, rose 1.3 percent last year after a meagre 0.2 percent gain in 1995. Unit labour costs rose 1.8 percent last year and 2.4 percent in 1995.
Some economists believe that government data have understated real productivity gains as the U.S. economy has become more service-oriented.
The Fed, the nation's central bank, last raised short-term interest rates on March 25, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation. They have held rates steady since.

In the second quarter, non-farm output rose at a 2.3 percent rate, down from 5.6 percent in the first quarter, while workers' hours rose at a 1.7 percent pace, down from 4.2 percent in the first quarter, the department said.
Inflation-adjusted hourly compensation, which includes the cost of employee benefits, rose at a 2 percent rate in the quarter, down from 2.1 percent in the first quarter.
In the manufacturing sector, productivity rose at a 3.2 percent pace in the quarter, up from 2.5 percent, while unit labour costs fell at a 0.4 percent rate after rising at a 1.8 percent rate.

Productivity at non-financial corporations, which excludes banks, brokerage firms and finance and insurance agencies, was revised down to a 1.9 percent gain in the first quarter, the most recent period for which data were available, from a previously estimated 4.6 percent gain.
